context:
Patient: 67M with 6 wk epigastric/LUQ pain, drenching night sweats and 8 kg weight loss; ECOG 2, T2DM on metformin, taking ibuprofen 400 mg QID. PET-CT: 9.4 cm retroperitoneal/mesenteric mass plus FDG-avid R kidney, L adrenal and liver lesions; GCB DLBCL (MYC 20%, BCL2 30%, FISH negative), marrow negative, LDH 1,290, uric acid 10.4, creatinine 1.1 -> 1.5.
What this case tests: Kidney, adrenal and liver lesions are extranodal organ disease, so stage IV, IPI 5/5 and CNS-IPI 6/6. | MYC 20% / BCL2 30% with negative FISH: neither double-expressor nor double-hit, so no intensified regimen such as DA-EPOCH-R. | ECOG 2 is disease-related in a patient who wants cure: full-dose Pola-R-CHP (or R-CHOP) x6 after a steroid prephase, not mini-CHOP or palliation. | Uric acid 10.4, LDH >5x ULN and rising creatinine mean high TLS risk: IV hydration, rasburicase after G6PD check, TLS labs every 6-12 hours for the first 72 hours, stop NSAIDs. | High CNS risk: MRI brain and LP with CSF cytology/flow now; HD-MTX only as an individualized option once renal function recovers and NSAIDs are stopped.

answer.diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified, germinal-center B-cell type by Hans algorithm (CD10+, MUM1/IRF4 negative), newly diagnosed and untreated. Core biopsy of the retroperitoneal mass (collected 2026-09-10, final 2026-09-12): CD20+, PAX5+, BCL6+, CD10+; CD3-, CD5-, CD30-, cyclin D1-, EBER-negative. FISH addendum (2026-09-16) negative for MYC, BCL2 and BCL6 rearrangements. Bone marrow (2026-09-11) without lymphoma on morphology, immunostains or flow. Clinically aggressive: 6-week pain, B symptoms, LDH 5x ULN and rising, bulky disease.
answer.stage: Ann Arbor stage IV-B (Lugano 2014 IV-B). Nodal disease: conglomerate retroperitoneal (para-aortic/aortocaval) and mesenteric mass 9.4 x 6.8 cm, SUVmax 24.1, encasing aorta and IVC without occlusion (bulky, 7.5 cm or more). Extranodal disease: right renal cortical lesion 3.2 cm (SUVmax 19.6), left adrenal 2.6 cm (SUVmax 17.2), hepatic segment VI 1.8 cm (SUVmax 15.0). The hepatic lesion is non-contiguous, so stage IV holds regardless of the renal and adrenal lesions. B symptoms present: unintentional weight loss 79 to 70.2 kg (about 11% in about 2 months) and drenching night sweats; measured temperatures 37.6-37.9 C, below the 38.0 C fever threshold. No supradiaphragmatic FDG-avid disease; 4 mm right upper lobe nodule, not FDG-avid, indeterminate, does not change stage (follow on restaging CT). Marrow negative. The liver lesion has not been biopsied. If it were not lymphoma, the stage would be III-B. Treatment is the same either way.
answer.biology: GCB-type DLBCL with high proliferation (Ki-67 about 70%). Double-expressor status is negative by IHC: MYC 20% (threshold 40%) and BCL2 30% (threshold 50%). FISH is negative for MYC, BCL2 and BCL6 rearrangements, so this is not double-hit or triple-hit lymphoma. There is no biologic reason for dose-adjusted EPOCH-R or for a high-grade B-cell regimen. GCB cell of origin is favorable with R-CHOP-type therapy, but the favorable effect is outweighed by the high clinical risk (IPI 5). Beta-2 microglobulin is 4.8 mg/L (elevated). EBV-negative. Hepatitis B core antibody negative, surface antibody positive (vaccine pattern), HCV and HIV negative. TP53 status is not on file and is not needed for the first-line decision. The renal, adrenal and hepatic lesions are PET-avid (SUVmax 15-20) and in keeping with lymphoma; a second primary such as renal cell carcinoma is very unlikely given the lymphoma core diagnosis, so no separate biopsy is needed unless these lesions fail to respond.
answer.prognosis: Treatment intent is curative, but this is high-risk disease. IPI 5 (age >60, LDH >ULN, ECOG >=2, stage IV, more than one extranodal site) is high risk; IPI 4 would still be high risk even if ECOG is 1. NCCN-IPI is in the high-risk group (by my count about 9, with LDH above 3x ULN and ECOG 2 contributing most). CNS-IPI is high (see cns_risk). Adverse features: 9.4 cm bulk, B symptoms, LDH 1,120 rising to 1,290 U/L (5.7x ULN), uric acid 10.4 mg/dL and rising, creatinine progression (eGFR 72 in 07/2025 to 50 now), albumin 3.1 g/dL, beta-2 microglobulin 4.8 mg/L. My estimate, with uncertainty: about 50-60% long-term survival with the planned regimen; 2-year PFS in the mid-to-high 60s to 70s percent range. Polatuzumab-containing therapy improved 2-year PFS by about 6-7 points overall in POLARIX (76.7% vs 70.2%), with consistent benefit across IPI subgroups in exploratory analysis, though the high-IPI subgroup is small. Prognosis is driven mainly by end-of-treatment PET response and by whether he can receive the planned dose intensity.
answer.first_line_treatment: Full-dose curative-intent immunochemotherapy: pola-R-CHP (polatuzumab vedotin replaces vincristine in R-CHOP), 21-day cycles, 6 cycles, with CNS prophylaxis and primary G-CSF prophylaxis. Per cycle (recalculate on C1D1 with actual weight; BSA about 1.85 m2 at 70 kg): polatuzumab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg IV day 1 (about 125 mg); rituximab 375 mg/m2 IV day 1 (about 690 mg); cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m2 IV day 1 (about 1,390 mg; no mesna needed at this dose); doxorubicin 50 mg/m2 IV day 1 (about 93 mg; cumulative 300 mg/m2 over 6 cycles); prednisone 100 mg PO days 1-5. Intrathecal methotrexate 12 mg on day 1 of each cycle, after a negative pre-treatment LP and with platelets 50 or more; number of doses per institutional protocol (I would plan one per cycle, 6 doses). Pegfilgrastim (or on-body injector) each cycle. Reasons: this is high-risk DLBCL and pola-R-CHP is a standard first-line option for IPI 2-5 per POLARIX. Fallback if polatuzumab is not approved or covered: R-CHOP-21 x6 with the same IT methotrexate and G-CSF, with no change in intensity. Not chosen: high-dose methotrexate, because eGFR is about 50 and falling and renal clearance is not reliable enough; dose-adjusted EPOCH-R, because there is no double-hit biology; reduced-intensity regimens, because he is fit enough for full dose (see fitness_and_goals). Timing: target C1D1 about 2026-09-25, once the pre-treatment items in pretreatment_workup are done, and do not delay for the wedding. Admit for cycle 1 for tumor lysis prophylaxis (see supportive_care). Radiotherapy is not indicated now; see response_assessment for consolidation to the bulky retroperitoneal site.
answer.cns_risk: High risk of CNS relapse. CNS-IPI high: age >60, LDH >ULN, ECOG >=2, stage IV, more than one extranodal site, and kidney and adrenal involvement (all six factors present; high-risk group is 4 or more points). Kidney and adrenal involvement, high IPI and bulky disease all favor CNS prophylaxis. Decision: give intrathecal methotrexate prophylaxis with each cycle, starting cycle 1. Before the first dose: brain MRI with and without gadolinium (a group II agent is acceptable at eGFR 50) and LP with cell count, cytology, flow cytometry, protein and glucose. Spine MRI only if back pain, radicular symptoms or paraspinal/epidural disease appear; none is documented. No testicular or paranasal risk features on exam or PET. Why intrathecal rather than high-dose methotrexate: high-dose methotrexate needs reliable renal clearance; his eGFR is 50 and declining, with recent NSAID exposure and an ACE inhibitor, so the nephrotoxicity risk is too high. Limits: the benefit of intrathecal methotrexate in DLBCL is not established by randomized data, and the approximately 10% CNS relapse risk in the high-CNS-IPI group is reduced, not eliminated. If brain MRI or CSF shows lymphoma, the plan changes to CNS-directed therapy with specialist input. Symptoms of CNS disease (headache, confusion, focal deficit, visual change) prompt urgent MRI and LP.
answer.response_assessment: Baseline reference: FDG PET-CT 2026-09-05 (SUVmax 24.1 for the dominant nodal mass). Ask nuclear medicine for a Deauville score and sum of the product of diameters for the target lesions so that later scans can be compared against them; these are not reported. Interim PET-CT after cycle 2 for prognosis and documentation. Outside a trial I would not change therapy for an interim result alone. End-of-treatment PET-CT about 4-6 weeks after cycle 6 (about late January to early February 2027), read by Lugano 2014 criteria: complete metabolic response = Deauville 1-3 with no new lesions; partial response = Deauville 4-5 with reduced uptake and residual masses. Residual PET-avid retroperitoneal disease at end of treatment: consolidative involved-site radiotherapy (about 30-36 Gy) to the bulky site, and biopsy if the residual uptake is high or new. Progression at end of treatment: biopsy, then salvage (for example R-GDP or R-ICE) with CAR-T assessment; he is unlikely to be a transplant candidate at age 67 with ECOG 2. Monitoring at each cycle: CBC with differential, CMP, LDH, uric acid, phosphate, creatinine and potassium. Restaging CT chest or follow-up of the 4 mm right upper lobe nodule at end of treatment. Surveillance after completion: clinic visit and labs every 3 months for 2 years, then less often; routine surveillance imaging is not recommended, imaging only for symptoms. What would change the plan: failure to reduce LDH or a rise in creatinine during cycle 1, an LVEF decline, grade 2 or higher neuropathy (pola), or cytopenias that delay cycles.
answer.pretreatment_workup:
Items to complete before C1D1, most within the next 3-5 days:
1. Brain MRI with and without contrast, and LP with cell count, cytology, flow, protein and glucose (platelets 145 is acceptable for LP; need 50 or more for intrathecal dosing).
2. Quantitative G6PD activity before rasburicase (and before dapsone if ever used).
3. Renal: urinalysis with microscopy, urine protein:creatinine ratio, renal and bladder ultrasound to exclude obstruction from the encasing retroperitoneal mass (no hydronephrosis on CT 08/15 and PET 09/05, but creatinine has risen since), and repeat BMP, magnesium, phosphate, uric acid and LDH within 48 hours of admission.
4. Coagulation panel (PT/INR, aPTT, fibrinogen), type and screen, and 12-lead ECG.
5. Central venous port placement before cycle 1 (doxorubicin is a vesicant; six cycles; 45-minute travel).
6. Lipase (epigastric pain, not on file), and repeat CBC with reticulocytes, iron studies, ferritin, B12 and folate for Hb 9.9.
7. Stool occult blood (NSAID exposure, epigastric pain, falling Hb).
8. Urinalysis and blood cultures if temperature reaches 38.0 C; low-grade temperatures and night sweats need an infection screen.
9. Hepatitis B: HBsAg and anti-HBc negative, anti-HBs positive. No HBV prophylaxis and no HBV DNA monitoring needed for rituximab.
10. Vaccines: inactivated influenza now, COVID-19 and pneumococcal if due; no live vaccines. Do not delay cycle 1 for vaccine response.
11. Baseline neuropathy exam and foot exam (diabetes; pola-R-CHP is neurotoxic).
12. Geriatric assessment (G8 or equivalent) and re-documented ECOG, since he is resting much of the afternoon.
13. Prior authorization for polatuzumab vedotin.
14. Dietitian, social work (transport, lodging, financial), PT, and teaching on fever and neutropenia precautions with the wife and daughter.
answer.supportive_care:
1. Stop ibuprofen today and avoid all NSAIDs. Scheduled acetaminophen 650 mg PO every 6 hours (maximum 3 g/day) for pain. For breakthrough pain, low-dose oxycodone 2.5-5 mg PO every 4 hours as needed (avoid morphine and codeine at this eGFR), with a bowel regimen. Low-dose palliative radiotherapy if pain stays uncontrolled after the first cycle.
2. Kidney protection: hold lisinopril during admission and hydration; restart when creatinine is back near 1.1-1.3 and potassium is 5.0 or below. Avoid IV contrast unless it is essential. Renally dose all new drugs.
3. Tumor lysis and hyperuricemia (high risk: uric acid 10.4 and rising, LDH 5.7x ULN, bulky disease, reduced eGFR): start allopurinol 100 mg PO daily now (renally reduced dose). Send G6PD now. If G6PD is normal, give rasburicase 0.2 mg/kg IV once before chemotherapy (day -1 or day 1). If G6PD is deficient, use allopurinol with hydration and daily uric acid and creatinine, and discuss with the team before cycle 1. Admit for cycle 1 from day -1 to day 3 for IV hydration (target urine output at least 100 mL/m2/h, watching volume given grade I diastolic dysfunction and EF 60%), electrolytes every 8-12 hours, and no potassium supplements. Hold cycle 1 if potassium is 6.0 or higher, or if creatinine rises by 0.3 mg/dL or more despite prophylaxis.
4. Antiemetics: NK1 antagonist plus 5-HT3 antagonist plus olanzapine 5 mg at bedtime. Minimize additional dexamethasone because prednisone is already given. Check QTc on ECG before ondansetron.
5. Gout: no NSAIDs or colchicine at full dose. Continue allopurinol. Low-dose colchicine prophylaxis at renally adjusted dose through cycles 1-2 (avoid if CrCl falls below 30). Treat any flare with a short oral prednisone course or intra-articular steroid.
6. Diabetes with steroid-induced hyperglycemia: glucose before meals and at bedtime during prednisone days; basal plus correction insulin or NPH with prednisone; target 140-180 mg/dL; endocrinology referral. Hold metformin during admission, dehydration, vomiting, AKI and any IV contrast; restart once eating normally and creatinine is stable (at eGFR 30-45 the maximum is 1,000 mg/day).
7. GI protection: pantoprazole 40 mg PO daily during steroid courses and while recovering from NSAID exposure. Report melena or hematemesis immediately.
8. PJP prophylaxis: atovaquone 1,500 mg PO daily with food through completion of chemotherapy. Avoid TMP-SMX (sulfonamide antibiotic rash in 2009; potassium 5.0; renal function; methotrexate interaction). Dapsone is not preferred.
9. Infection and neutropenia: primary pegfilgrastim prophylaxis each cycle (age 65 or older, ECOG 2, renal impairment, diabetes; febrile neutropenia risk above 20%). Fever of 38.0 C or higher means immediate call and ED evaluation with cultures. No routine antibacterial prophylaxis unless ANC is expected below 0.5 for 7 days or more.
10. Anemia (Hb 9.9): transfuse for Hb below 7 g/dL, or below 8 with symptoms or cardiac ischemia. Iron repletion if iron-deficient. No erythropoiesis-stimulating agent in curative-intent therapy.
11. Thrombosis: no routine prophylaxis. Monitor for DVT given IVC encasement, steroids and the port; if DVT occurs, enoxaparin with renal-appropriate dosing (no adjustment needed at CrCl about 47 mL/min).
12. Nutrition: albumin 3.1 with about 11% weight loss; dietitian referral and oral supplements, monitoring glucose with supplements.
13. Cardiac: baseline LVEF 60% with GLS -19%; cumulative doxorubicin 300 mg/m2. Repeat echo only if symptoms or for institutional practice. Manage hypertension and diabetes as cardiac risk reduction.
14. Neuropathy: examine before each cycle; hold polatuzumab for grade 2 or higher neuropathy.
15. Logistics: local laboratory draws between visits, telehealth for in-between checks, a 24-hour triage number for fever, and a caregiver plan with the wife and daughter.
answer.fitness_and_goals: Fitness: ECOG 2 documented 09/02; he is independent in self-care and walks around the house, but rests much of the afternoon, so he is borderline 2 versus 3. Re-document ECOG and do a geriatric assessment before C1D1. Comorbidities: T2DM (HbA1c 7.4%), hypertension (controlled, 122/74), progressive kidney impairment (eGFR 50, creatinine 1.5; Cockcroft-Gault CrCl about 47 mL/min at 70 kg), gout (untreated), hyperlipidemia, BPH, former smoker (30 pack-years), LVEF 60% with grade I diastolic dysfunction, normal bilirubin and transaminases. Decision: he is fit enough for full-dose curative-intent immunochemotherapy with G-CSF and CNS prophylaxis; age 67 is not in itself a reason for dose reduction, and comorbidity drives the supportive plan (no high-dose methotrexate, renal dosing, tumor lysis prophylaxis, steroid glucose control). If ECOG is confirmed as 3 or the geriatric assessment shows frailty, I would discuss a modified-intensity regimen with him and his family before cycle 1 rather than delay treatment. Goals: he wants treatment aimed at cure, which is consistent with this plan. Wedding: if C1D1 is about 09/25, cycle 4 starts about 11/27, and mid-December falls around days 15-21 of cycle 4 or day 1 of cycle 5. Attendance is realistic if counts have recovered and he has no active infection, but I cannot promise it. Advise infection precautions (avoid crowds and sick contacts, masks), plan rest, and check counts before he travels. Do not delay chemotherapy to fit the date. Logistics: the 45-minute drive and his wife's driving are a real burden; plan local labs, telehealth for in-between visits, and cycle-day visits with a plan for each one. Confirm a health care proxy (wife or daughter), document code status, and revisit goals after each restaging.
missing_information: Brain MRI and CSF results (LP and cytology) have not been done; both are needed before intrathecal methotrexate.
G6PD activity is not on file; needed before rasburicase.
Renal ultrasound, urinalysis with microscopy and urine protein:creatinine ratio are not on file; obstruction and intrinsic renal involvement are not excluded for the creatinine rise.
Actual urine output and volume status since the NSAID escalation are not documented.
Hepatic lesion was not biopsied; the stage is presumed IV-B on PET (III-B if the lesion were not lymphoma).
Baseline Deauville score and sum of target-lesion measurements are not in the PET report.
Current ECOG is not re-documented since 09/02; a geriatric assessment (G8 or equivalent) has not been done.
Lipase, coagulation panel, fibrinogen, ECG, stool occult blood, reticulocyte count and iron studies are not on file.
Baseline peripheral neuropathy exam is not documented (diabetes; polatuzumab is neurotoxic).
Insurance coverage and prior authorization for polatuzumab vedotin are not documented.

The 4 mm right upper lobe nodule has no follow-up plan yet; it needs follow-up on restaging imaging.
TP53 status and VZV serology are not on file; neither changes the first-line decision.

items.criterion: The response states the diagnosis is diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (NOS) with a germinal-center B-cell (GCB) phenotype.
The response stages the disease as Lugano/Ann Arbor stage IV.
The response attributes stage IV to extranodal organ involvement of the kidney, adrenal gland and liver.
The response notes B symptoms (night sweats and/or weight loss >10% or fevers).
The response assigns this patient a stage lower than IV (stage I, II or III).
The response states the lymphoma is neither double-expressor (MYC 20%, BCL2 30% below thresholds) nor double-hit (FISH negative for MYC, BCL2 and BCL6 rearrangements).
The response classifies this lymphoma as double-hit / high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements.
The response classifies this lymphoma as double-expressor.
The response calculates IPI as 5 (or explicitly high-risk IPI 4-5): age >60, elevated LDH, ECOG >=2, stage IV, >1 extranodal site.
The response calculates CNS-IPI as 6 or high risk (4-6), counting kidney/adrenal involvement.
The response recommends curative-intent full-dose immunochemotherapy with Pola-R-CHP or R-CHOP for 6 cycles.
The response names Pola-R-CHP as the preferred regimen given IPI >=2 (R-CHOP acceptable alternative).
The response recommends a steroid prephase (e.g. prednisone ~100 mg daily for 5-7 days) before cycle 1 given age >60, ECOG 2 and high tumor burden.
The response recommends palliative-only treatment, best supportive care, or hospice as the plan.
The response recommends DA-EPOCH-R or another intensified regimen for this patient.
The response recommends a dose-reduced regimen (e.g. R-mini-CHOP) as the initial plan, despite age 67 and disease-related ECOG 2.
The response identifies a high risk of CNS relapse driven by kidney/adrenal involvement and high CNS-IPI.
The response recommends baseline CNS evaluation: contrast MRI brain and lumbar puncture with CSF cytology and flow cytometry.
The response discusses CNS prophylaxis (e.g. high-dose methotrexate) as an individualized option with uncertain benefit and ties its feasibility to renal function / stopping NSAIDs.
The response schedules high-dose methotrexate immediately (e.g. with cycle 1) without addressing the rising creatinine, renal involvement, or concurrent NSAID use.
The response plans an end-of-treatment FDG PET-CT read with Lugano criteria / Deauville 5-point scale.
The response says residual Deauville 4-5 uptake at end of treatment should be biopsied if it would change management.

The response recognizes high tumor-lysis risk (uric acid 10.4, LDH >5x ULN, rising creatinine) and orders TLS prophylaxis with IV hydration, a uric-acid-lowering agent and frequent TLS labs (every 6-12 hours for the first 72 hours; daily is not frequent enough at this risk).
The response favors rasburicase (given hyperuricemia with renal impairment) and checks G6PD before giving it.
The response recommends primary G-CSF prophylaxis (e.g. pegfilgrastim) with each cycle, given age >=65.
The response stops ibuprofen/NSAIDs (nephrotoxic with rising creatinine; interacts with methotrexate) and offers alternative analgesia.
The response anticipates steroid-induced hyperglycemia in this diabetic patient (glucose monitoring / insulin plan) or adjusts metformin for falling eGFR.
The response confirms hepatitis B serology was checked (HBsAg and anti-HBc nonreactive) so no antiviral prophylaxis is needed before rituximab.
The response notes the baseline LVEF of 60% permits anthracycline.
The response judges ECOG 2 as disease-related and not a reason to de-escalate curative therapy, and acknowledges the patient's goal of cure.
